title: Data Structures

entries.meaning: A way of organising related data plus the operations allowed on it.
A linear structure with last-in-first-out access: push and pop at one end, the top.
An expression with each operator written after its operands; it is evaluated with a stack and needs no parentheses.
entries.citationQuote: Applications of stacks: infix-to-postfix transformation, evaluating postfix expressions

entries.meaning: A linear structure with first-in-first-out access: insertion at the rear, deletion at the front.
A queue stored in a fixed array whose rear wraps to index 0, reusing slots freed at the front.
entries.citationQuote: Types of queues: de-queue, circular queue

entries.meaning: A chain of nodes, each holding data and one pointer to the next node; the last pointer is null.
entries.citationQuote: Singly linked list: memory representation, insertion and deletion at first, in-between and end

entries.meaning: A tree in which each node has at most two children, called left and right.
entries.citationQuote: Trees: basic terminology; binary tree concepts

entries.meaning: Visiting a graph level by level from a source using a queue; depth-first uses a stack or recursion.
